strengths: Addresses a critical gap: First large-scale, human-validated dataset of LLM-generated proofs, filling a clear need in the field
Exceptionally rigorous methodology: Expert judges (IMO participants), careful pilot phase with 35% double-grading, high inter-rater agreement (90.4%), and thoughtful interface design
Substantial scale and scope: 5,062 proofs across 1,010 problems from multiple prestigious competitions, covering 6 state-of-the-art models
Addresses important open questions: Resolves debates on formal vs. informal proofs (4× gap), final-answer accuracy gaps (O3 drops 30%), and best-of-n effectiveness (improves to 47%)
Demonstrates practical utility: Fine-tuned OPC-R1-8B achieves 88.1% accuracy, matching frontier models and approaching human-level performance (90.4%)
Excellent reproducibility: Complete dataset release, all prompts documented, detailed methodology, code with instructions, grading interface provided
Thoughtful treatment of limitations: Contamination analysis, out-of-distribution evaluation, uncertainty mechanisms, and comprehensive validation procedures
Rich qualitative analysis: Documents common failure modes (inequality handling, synthetic geometry reasoning, overgeneralization) with concrete examples
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: Primarily a dataset contribution; evaluation approach is straightforward binary correctness judgments; fine-tuning uses standard GRPO without novel techniques
Scope constraints: 84% high-school competition problems; limited coverage of advanced/research-level mathematics; mostly closed-form problems not representative of open mathematical research
Model coverage timing issues: GROK-4 and GPT-5 only included as judges, not provers; dataset constructed before their release; inconsistent model coverage across problems

Contamination cannot be fully ruled out: While competition-based analysis suggests difficulty dominates, authors acknowledge GEMINI-2.5-PRO vs O4-MINI gap 'cannot be conclusively attributed to genuine performance differences'
Best-of-n evaluation limitations: Only 152 problems in subset (60 with all 8 generations), large confidence intervals, single-model evaluation (O4-MINI), bug in Rank (Swiss) excluded 18 samples
OPC-R1-8B performance caveats: Training and test sets share distribution (both high-school level); main result (88.1%) may somewhat overestimate generalization despite reasonable OOD performance
Incomplete human baseline: Derived from ~10% double-graded subset rather than test set; potential systematic differences between human and LLM judges not thoroughly explored
Analysis depth: Limited investigation of which mathematical skills are hardest; brief treatment of problem-category effects (§C.2); formal proof comparison limited to single model
